## fix(llm): OPENAI_BASE_URL fails CLOSED on a malformed value, and the guard's contract is pinned by request destination

### Defect
`app/services/llm_provider.py` validates `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for every `AsyncOpenAI` factory (openai_service x3, extraction_service, url_extraction_service).

- **origin/main:** a malformed value makes `provider_base_url()` return `None`. openai-python 3.3.1 then re-reads the variable itself (`if base_url is None: base_url = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL")`), so the client is built against the malformed value while the log says "using stock OpenAI". A blank or whitespace value does the same, which gives base_url `''` / `%20%20%20/`, and every request fails. An explicit stock URL is labelled `openai-compatible@...`.
- **This PR's first cut (0b7b9b8c):** a malformed value was swapped for stock OpenAI. With sockets blocked, measurement showed this **fails OPEN**. `not-a-url`, `//proto`, `junk value` and the likeliest real typo, `api.gateway.test/v1`, all resolved `api.openai.com`. A mistyped gateway URL would therefore have sent the configured key and the users' prompts to OpenAI, the provider the operator was routing away from, with only a WARNING. The first cut also rejected valid URLs with an upper- or mixed-case scheme (`HTTPS://UPPER.test/v1`, which works on main) and sent them to OpenAI too. Its `describe_provider()` echoed URL userinfo (`openai-compatible@https://user:sk-pw@gw.test/v1`), contradicting its own docstring.

### Fix (the only files changed are `app/services/llm_provider.py` and `tests/test_llm_provider_base_url.py`)
- Unset, blank or whitespace -> the EXPLICIT stock URL `https://api.openai.com/v1`, never `None`, so the SDK cannot re-read the variable.
- A valid http(s) URL -> returned with surrounding whitespace stripped and the scheme lower-cased. The scheme check is case-insensitive.
- Any other non-blank value -> **FAIL CLOSED**. The value is returned unchanged (whitespace-stripped), so httpx refuses the request at request time (`openai.APIConnectionError` <- `UnsupportedProtocol`) before any DNS lookup or connect. It is never swapped for stock OpenAI. One `logger.error` per call names `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, with the value redacted to `len=N, starts='<first 8 chars>'`.
- `is_custom_provider()` is True only for a valid, non-stock http(s) endpoint. Stock is recognised in any spelling (scheme/host case, trailing slash).
- `describe_provider()` returns `openai` for stock, `openai-compatible@<url>` with userinfo, query and fragment stripped, and `misconfigured:OPENAI_BASE_URL` for a malformed value, which is never echoed. It computes `provider_base_url()` once, so there is one log line per call.
- The stale docstrings ("unset -> None ... byte-identical", "constructed exactly as before") were rewritten to the contract above. The unused `Optional` import was removed.

### Evidence (pinned venv: openai 3.3.1, httpx 0.28.1, pytest 9.1.1, fastapi 0.141.1)
- **Unit file: 54 passed / 0 failed.** An autouse guard blocks every non-loopback `getaddrinfo`/`connect`, disables proxies, and fails a test on any attempt it does not take. The destination tests drive a real `AsyncOpenAI` request and assert which host was attempted:

  - `{gateway.test}`, `{upper.test}` and `{mixed.test}` for valid URLs, including padded and upper/mixed-case schemes.
  - No attempt at all for 6 malformed values and for all four real app factories.
- **Log line pinned:** exactly one ERROR, naming OPENAI_BASE_URL, redacted, with no credential tail. There is one per `provider_base_url` / `describe_provider` / `is_custom_provider` call, and none for unset or valid values.

  - Unset -> None: 9.
  - No strip: 8.
  - Double logging: 2.

- **RED demonstrations with the same test file** (the module swapped under its real dotted name, no ImportError; STOCK_OPENAI_BASE_URL and is_custom_provider resolved by getattr fallback):
  - origin/main's module: **31 failed**. These cover the blank/whitespace destination, stock labels, credentials in the label, the malformed label/return/log level, and the unset-returns-explicit-stock spy.
  - The first cut's module: **32 failed + 6 guard errors**. These cover the fail-closed destination, the uppercase destination, trailing-slash stock and credentials.

### Flag / env state
There is no feature flag; the lever is `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, read on every call. With it unset, the effect is identical to the SDK default: `client.base_url` is `https://api.openai.com/v1/` and requests go to api.openai.com. The only difference is the SDK's private `_base_url_was_default` (False vs True), which openai 3.3.1 reads only on a workload-identity mode switch; the app configures no workload identity, so it is inert. **UNVERIFIED:** "OPENAI_BASE_URL is unset on both Railway services, so prod behaviour is unchanged" is carried over from the original PR and was NOT measured this round (Railway was not read). ### Honest limits
- Fail-closed is a request-time failure, not a construction-time raise. The app still boots, and every LLM call fails with APIConnectionError until the variable is fixed or unset. - The redacted log keeps the first 8 characters. For a malformed value shaped like `user:pwd@host`, those 8 characters can include part of a short credential. That is what the redaction ruling specifies.

- This branch sits on origin/main b203cfcc. origin/main has since moved to 41ec7d5f, a mobile W3-15 change plus docs, which does not touch the two files here or the three client factories. It has not been re-rebased.

## fix(price): Gents/Ladies wrong-gender leak, with the strict gender taking precedence (PR#32 extension)

### Defect
With the variant-descriptor axes on, a title that says "Gents" and one that says "Ladies" were matched as the same product: `_selection_match('Ajmal Aristocrat Gents', 'Ajmal Aristocrat Ladies', 'fragrances')` returned True. `gents` and `ladies` are fragrance padding tokens, so the subset check ignores them. They were also missing from both the strict gender sets and `_pronoun_gender_of`, so the gender-contradiction axis never saw them. This is the same bug PR#32 fixed for him/her.

### Fix
1. **The words.** `_pronoun_gender_of` now maps `gents` to men and `ladies` to women (`_PRONOUN_MEN_TOKENS` / `_PRONOUN_WOMEN_TOKENS`). Matching is by whole word after `_fold_identity`, so `Gentleman`, `Gentlemen`, `Gladiator`, `Cher` and `Hermes` never trigger it. It feeds only the contradiction axis. `_gender_of` stays strict, so the rule that a women's query must be confirmed by the candidate (the femme asymmetry) and the identity logic are unchanged.
2. **The strict gender takes precedence (review fix).** `_vd_gender_mismatch` now computes `g = d.gender or d.gender_pronoun` on both sides, so the pronoun gender is used only when the strict gender is None. Without this, a strict-gender title that also carried a stray opposite retailer word became "ambiguous". Main rejected these contradictions, but the first version of this PR accepted them at both the selection gate and the display/cache-read check (`backstop_identity_verdict`):
   - 'Versace Eros Pour Homme' vs 'Versace Eros Pour Femme - Gents'
   - 'Dior Sauvage For Men' vs 'Dior Sauvage For Women Gents'
   - 'Versace Eros Pour Femme' vs 'Versace Eros Pour Homme Ladies' (backstop)

   All three are rejected again, as `not_exact:gender`. The same change also closes an older PR#32 case: 'Versace Eros Pour Homme' vs 'Versace Eros Pour Femme For Him' is now rejected (with the flag on).

### Scope
The contradiction axis runs for fragrances, makeup, skincare, haircare and fashion. With the flag on, Gents/Ladies therefore also reject outside fragrance. Examples, pinned in the tests: Casio Edifice Gents vs Ladies Watch (fashion) and Carolina Herrera 212 Men vs 212 Ladies (makeup), at both call sites. In the probes the category "other" also changed at selection, from accept to reject, for opposite-gender pairs. Electronics has no gender axis (pinned).

The price-identity gate matched a fragrance "<X> Gents" against "<X> Ladies" as the same product. `_selection_match('Ajmal Aristocrat Gents', 'Ajmal Aristocrat Ladies', 'fragrances')` returned True on main with both gates on, so a men's query could be priced from the women's PDP. `gents` and `ladies` are in `_FRAGRANCE_PADDING_TOKENS`, which the subset check ignores. They were missing from the strict `_GENDER_*_TOKENS` sets and from `_pronoun_gender_of`, so the gender contradiction axis never fired for them. PR #32 fixed exactly this for him/her.

### Fix
1. `_pronoun_gender_of` now maps `gents -> men` and `ladies -> women`, beside him/her. It is the separate, flag-gated pronoun axis that feeds only the contradiction check (`_vd_gender_mismatch`, via `VariantDescriptor.gender_pronoun`). `_gender_of` stays strict, so the femme asymmetry and the empty-core/identity logic are unchanged. Tokens are word-level after `_fold_identity`: Gent's, Ladies', full-width Ｇｅｎｔｓ and upper case fold to the token, and Gentleman, Gentlemen, Gentsx and Sladies do not trigger it. A title carrying both genders ("Ladies & Gents", "for Him and Her") resolves to None, so it is ambiguous and never a contradiction.
2. **Strict gender wins** (found in adversarial review, one line in `_vd_gender_mismatch`). The pronoun gender is consulted only when the strict gender is None: `g = d.gender or d.gender_pronoun`, on both sides. The PR #32 helper treated "strict gender + opposite catalogue word" as ambiguous. With gents/ladies added, that opened a new leak: 'Versace Eros Pour Homme' vs 'Versace Eros Pour Femme - Gents' and 'Dior Sauvage For Men' vs 'Dior Sauvage For Women Gents' passed selection and the backstop, and 'Eros Pour Femme' vs 'Eros Pour Homme Ladies' passed `backstop_identity_verdict`. All three are rejected again at both call sites (backstop -> `(False, 'not_exact:gender')`) and are pinned.

### Scope (wider than fragrances)
The contradiction axis runs for fragrances, makeup, skincare, haircare and fashion. Gents/Ladies therefore also reject in beauty and fashion: Casio Edifice Gents vs Ladies Watch, and Carolina Herrera 212 Men vs 212 Ladies in makeup. ### Defect
`app/services/llm_provider.py` validates `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for every `AsyncOpenAI` factory: `extraction_service.get_client`, `url_extraction_service.get_client`, and `openai_service.get_client` in both its shared and dedicated forms. On origin/main it has three problems:
- A malformed value makes `provider_base_url()` return `None`. The SDK then re-reads the variable itself (openai 3.3.1 `_client.py`: `if base_url is None: base_url = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL")`), so the value the module rejected is used anyway. Meanwhile the module logs "using stock OpenAI" and `describe_provider()` says `openai`.
- A blank or whitespace-only value reaches the SDK as `''`, `'%20%20%20/'`, or (for `'\t'`) an `InvalidURL` raised at construction. It is not treated as unset.
- The scheme check is case-sensitive. `HTTPS://UPPER.test/v1` is called malformed even though it works.

The PR's first cut replaced `None` with the stock URL. That made a malformed value fail OPEN. Measured with the network blocked: `api.gateway.test/v1`, the most likely typo (a gateway URL missing its scheme), sent the configured key and the users' prompts to api.openai.com. origin/main failed closed on it, by accident.

### Fix
- Unset, blank or whitespace-only: `provider_base_url()` returns the EXPLICIT stock URL `https://api.openai.com/v1`, never `None`.
- An `http://` or `https://` URL with a non-empty host: returned with the scheme lower-cased. The scheme match ignores case, and surrounding whitespace is stripped.
- Anything else is non-blank and malformed, and it FAILS CLOSED:
  - The raw value (stripped) is returned unchanged, so every client is built against it and every request fails at request time with `openai.APIConnectionError`.
  - Each call logs one `logger.error` that names `OPENAI_BASE_URL`. The value is redacted to its length and first 8 characters, because the raw value may carry userinfo.
  - Measured on openai 3.3.1 / httpx 0.28.1, there are three failure classes, and none reaches api.openai.com or the intended gateway:
    - No http(s) scheme (`not-a-url`, `api.gateway.test/v1`, `//proto`, `ftp://x`, `junk value`): `UnsupportedProtocol`, raised before any DNS lookup or connect.
    - An http(s) scheme but no host (`https://`, `http://`, `https:/gw.test/v1`, `HTTPS:/gw.test/v1`, `http:gw.test/v1`, `https:\\gw.test\v1`): one resolution attempt on an EMPTY host, then `ConnectError`.
    - An unparseable authority (`https://[gw.test/v1`): one resolution attempt on `%5bgw.test`, then `ConnectError`.
- `is_custom_provider()`: True only for a valid, non-stock URL. Every spelling of the stock URL (scheme and host case, trailing slash) counts as stock. A query string or fragment on api.openai.com/v1 makes it not stock.
- `describe_provider()`:
  - It returns `openai`, `openai-compatible@<url>`, or `misconfigured:OPENAI_BASE_URL`. A malformed value is never echoed.
  - The URL it shows has userinfo, query and fragment stripped. When an unencoded `/`, `?` or `#` in the password makes urlsplit cut the authority early, the whole location is shown as `<redacted>`.
